plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the two rotation operations on a binary search tree as a pair of small subtree drawings joined by dotted arrows. On the right, the upper node is a gray circle labeled x with a short stub edge rising to an unnamed parent; x's left edge ends at the Greek letter alpha, and its right edge descends to a second gray circle labeled y whose two edges end at beta and gamma. On the left stands the other configuration: y is now the upper node holding the parent stub, x is y's left child, and the edges terminate at alpha and beta below x and at gamma below y. Subtrees appear only as these labeled edges, without triangles. Between the drawings, an upper dotted arrow points leftward with "LEFT-ROTATE(T, x)" set above it, and a lower dotted arrow points rightward with "RIGHT-ROTATE(T, y)" set beneath it. Placing the before and after shapes side by side isolates what a rotation touches, the link joining x and y and which of them owns the middle subtree beta. The left-to-right order alpha, x, beta, y, gamma survives in both pictures, which is what makes the operation a legal local repair to the pointer structure.

interactionPlan.concept: A binary-search-tree rotation is a local pointer rearrangement that swaps the parent-child roles of x and y while preserving the inorder sequence α, x, β, y, γ.

interactions.label: Implement tree rotation

api.does: return node.left when side is 'left' and node.right when side is 'right'
return node.parent, or NIL if node is the root
assign node.left or node.right to child and record that pointer assignment as one animation frame
assign node.parent to parent and record that parent-pointer assignment as one animation frame

add a learner-visible note to the next replay frame without changing the tree

input.label: Initial local tree
input.default: direction=left; parent=P; x.left=α; x.right=y; y.left=β; y.right=γ

interactions.success_check: For a left rotation, y occupies x's former parent link, x is y.left, β is x.right, α remains x.left, γ remains y.right, all parent pointers are consistent, and the inorder order α, x, β, y, γ is unchanged; for a right rotation, the symmetric property holds.
interactions.teaches: The rotation is not a vague shape flip: it is a precise sequence of pointer assignments, especially moving β to the middle child position and then swapping which of x and y owns the parent link

interactions.label: Show inorder invariant
interactions.teaches: Even though the tree shape changes, the left-to-right search order α, x, β, y, γ is identical before and after the rotation

demo_steps.title: Start with the local subtree
demo_steps.narration: The active part of the tree contains only x, y, and three untouched subtrees α, β, and γ. A rotation will change only the links around x, y, β, and the parent stub.

demo_steps.title: Move the middle subtree β
demo_steps.narration: Step the code until β is reassigned. β is the only subtree that changes sides: in a left rotation it moves from y.left to x.right, and in a right rotation it moves from x.right to y.left.

demo_steps.title: Swap the parent-child roles
demo_steps.narration: Continue stepping: y takes x's former parent link in LEFT-ROTATE, while x becomes y's left child. RIGHT-ROTATE performs the exact inverse assignments.

demo_steps.title: Check the search-order invariant
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the invariant guide. The visual shape has changed, but an inorder traversal still encounters α, then x, then β, then y, then γ.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Rotation changes tree height and local shape by rewiring a few pointers, but it remains legal for a binary search tree because the inorder order α, x, β, y, γ never changes.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean black-and-white textbook style: gray circular nodes labeled x and y in italic math text, black edges, Greek subtree labels α, β, γ placed at edge tips rather than drawn as triangles. Preserve the original side-by-side comparison: the left drawing has y above x, and the right drawing has x above y. Put the dotted LEFT-ROTATE arrow above pointing left and the dotted RIGHT-ROTATE arrow below pointing right. During code replay, highlight changed pointers in a strong color such as red or orange, keep unchanged α and γ edges muted, and emphasize β with a distinct color as it moves between the two middle-child positions.

authoredContext: The search-tree operations TREE-INSERT and TREE-DELETE, when run on a redblack tree with n keys, take O.lg n/ time. Because they modify the tree, the result may violate the red-black properties enumerated in Section 13.1. To restore these properties, we must change the colors of some of the nodes in the tree and also change the pointer structure. We change the pointer structure through rotation, which is a local operation in a search tree that preserves the binary-search-tree property. Figure 13.2 shows the two kinds of rotations: left rotations and right rotations. When we do a left rotation on a node x, we assume that its right child y is not T:nil; x may be any node in the tree whose right child is not T:nil. The left rotation “pivots” around the link from x to y. It makes y the new root of the subtree, with x as y’s left child and y’s left child as x’s right child.

discrepancies: The main textbook diagram is squeezed into the left portion of the viewport by a large always-visible control/code panel, so the static figure is much smaller and less dominant than the source.
The dotted rotation arrows use single large filled triangular arrowheads, while the source uses small clustered chevron-like arrowheads on dotted lines.
The arrow/dash styling is visually heavier and less fine-grained than the source, especially in the rendered screenshot where the arrowheads dominate the center.
Some labels in the tree and rotation titles are noticeably smaller at the default rendered size than in the source, reducing the drop-in resemblance.
evaluation.notes: The tree topology, labels, and rotation concept are accurately reproduced, with strong pedagogical interactions, but the default rendered composition is too compressed and the rotation arrows differ noticeably from the textbook styling.
action_items: Make the default static diagram occupy most of the available width, either by docking the UI below/collapsing the code workbench initially or by enlarging the SVG diagram relative to the control panel.
Redraw the dotted rotation arrows with smaller clustered arrowheads matching the source rather than one large filled triangle at each arrow end.
Increase the on-figure tree labels and rotation-title sizes slightly for better match and readability at inline screenshot size.
Tune the dotted line dash pattern and stroke weight to look closer to the fine textbook dotted arrows.
